corrections.notes: ASH 2019 suggests corticosteroids over observation for adults with newly diagnosed ITP and a platelet count below 30 x 10^9/L, even with minor bleeding. Observation is for counts of at least 30.
corrections.source: American Society of Hematology 2019 guidelines for immune thrombocytopenia (Neunert et al, Blood Adv 2019)
corrections.newExplanation: In adults with newly diagnosed ITP and a platelet count below 30 x 10^9/L, ASH 2019 suggests corticosteroids rather than observation, even if bleeding is absent or minor. A short course of prednisone (no more than 6 weeks, including taper) or dexamethasone is preferred. Observation is suggested for asymptomatic adults with counts of 30 x 10^9/L or more. Patient anxiety alone isn't a reason to aim for a specific target, and platelet transfusion is reserved for serious bleeding. Source: American Society of Hematology 2019 guidelines for immune thrombocytopenia (Neunert et al, Blood Adv 2019)

corrections.notes: For adults with newly diagnosed ITP and platelets below 30 x 10^9/L, ASH 2019 suggests corticosteroids over observation. A count of 10 x 10^9/L in a 68-year-old warrants treatment.
corrections.source: American Society of Hematology 2019 guidelines for immune thrombocytopenia (Neunert et al, Blood Adv 2019)
corrections.newExplanation: ASH 2019 suggests corticosteroids over observation for adults with newly diagnosed ITP and a platelet count below 30 x 10^9/L, whatever the bleeding symptoms. At 10 x 10^9/L this patient should start prednisone (no more than 6 weeks including taper) or dexamethasone. IVIG is added when a rapid rise is needed, for example with significant bleeding. Bone marrow examination isn't routinely needed when the presentation is typical. Source: American Society of Hematology 2019 guidelines for immune thrombocytopenia (Neunert et al, Blood Adv 2019)
